proof.claim:
When every node starts at once from identical conditions, exactly one
authority must emerge.

THE FAULT. Stop all five nodes, then start all five simultaneously — one
docker invocation, not a sequence.

WHY SIMULTANEITY IS THE POINT. full-cluster-blackout already stops all three
etcd nodes and checks the cluster comes back. But a staggered restart lets one
node establish leadership before the others finish booting, which is the easy
case and the one that usually happens in practice. Starting together removes
that accident: five controllers race from the same starting line, every one of
them with a valid local view, none of them with any reason to defer.

That is when election races, duplicate join requests, duplicate workflow
dispatch and registration corruption become reachable. Each node has a
complete local state directory and no evidence that anyone else is also
starting.

WHAT MUST HOLD. One leader address, not several. Every node registered exactly
once. No duplicate or ambiguous artifacts from concurrent publish or
registration. No drift storm from several controllers each deciding the cluster
needs converging. And the cluster genuinely healthy afterwards rather than
merely responsive.

This is the most destructive scenario in the suite: it stops the entire
cluster. It is also the closest thing to a real datacentre power event, which
is exactly why staggering it would be testing the wrong thing.

authority.note: Simulation output is evidence/candidate knowledge only. Governed promotion is required before production may rely on it.
